fatal_errors: The proposed W/Mo addition does not reconstruct the target Zr intervention and does not specify a single element or dosage.
The base alloy composition, initial FCC/B2 microstructure, processing route, and quantitative untreated baseline are unspecified.
No prior evidence is cited to support simultaneous improvements in mechanical, creep, and corrosion behavior.

The predicted monotonic improvement misses the composition-dependent tradeoff: moderate Zr optimizes mechanical and creep properties, whereas higher Zr gives the best corrosion resistance but degrades mechanical performance.
The falsification rule permits one of the three claimed properties to worsen without falsifying the hypothesis, so it does not test the full claim.
explanation: The response recognizes the requested three-property objective and proposes elemental alloying with broadly plausible precipitation, boundary-pinning, and oxide-film mechanisms. However, it is too generic to constitute a testable materials hypothesis and does not match the Zr-alloyed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 system. It omits composition, dose, processing and test conditions, quantitative predictions, and evidence. Its experiment lacks specified refractory concentration, environmental conditions, creep protocol, and statistical thresholds, while its falsification criterion is inconsistent with the claim that all three properties improve.
